title: Anchored model flow: wires and microcopy (working)
content:
Purpose: capture a lightweight, actionable wireframe + microcopy draft for the ‘anchoring’ UX — i.e., users pinning model versions to endpoints (long-term anchors), short-term canary pins, and the catalog entry path that surfaces anchor status. This doc is intentionally informal: sketches, copy experiments, constraints, and open questions for grooming.

Context / problem framing:
- Customers want predictable behaviour when an endpoint is created: they expect the same model to be served (no silent drift) but also want the flexibility to adopt improvements.
- Current product language uses ‘pin’ and ‘freeze’ inconsistently across console and docs. Needs a single, less-ambiguous metaphor that surfaces intent (stability vs. upgrade) and lifetime.
- Need UI affordances for: pin lifetime, canary rollout, fallback policy, audit trail, and cost/throughput implications.

High level UX goals:
1) Make anchoring explicit at creation time (step in endpoint wizard) — user chooses either: unpinned (float to latest), anchored (pin to specific model version), or anchored-with-rollout (pin with scheduled upgrade/canary).
2) Reduce surprise: show clear labels in catalog and endpoint list for anchored endpoints (badge + hovercard).
3) Provide easy rollback and time-based expiry controls (pin-expires).
4) Surface performance/cost delta when selecting quantized/variant model for anchor.

Wireframe notes (screen-by-screen, rough):
A) Endpoint Creation — Step 3: Model selection (compact wire)
- Left: model catalog picker with search + filters (arch, seq-len, quantization, latency profile).
- Right: selection summary card (large) with: model name, version dropdown (defaults to ‘recommended’), pin toggle (off by default), pin options revealed when toggle on.
- Pin options (reveal area):
  * Radio: [ ] Anchor permanently (pin to this version)
           [ ] Anchor with scheduled upgrade (choose target version & schedule)
           [ ] Anchor temporarily (choose expiry: 7d / 30d / custom)
  * Small copy under radio: “Anchoring keeps this endpoint on a specific model version. Choose temporarily if you want automatic upgrades later.”
  * Inline cost/latency line: “Est. latency: 85ms (+12% vs latest) • Est tokens / $0.008/token” (pull from model profile).
- Primary CTA: Create endpoint (if pinned, show small badge on button: Create — anchored).

Copy variants for the pin toggle tooltip (A/B test candidates):
- V1: "Anchor this endpoint to the selected model version so outputs won’t change unexpectedly."
- V2: "Pin locks the endpoint to a chosen model version. You can schedule upgrades or set an expiry later."
- V3 (short): "Lock to version (prevents automatic upgrades)."

B) Endpoint list / catalog row badges
- Add compact badge to rows: "Anchored" (blue) or "Floating" (muted) with hovercard text:
  * Anchored hovercard: "This endpoint is pinned to v3.4.6 until 2026-03-01. Click to manage pins and rollouts."
  * Floating hovercard: "Follows the channel’s recommended version. May upgrade automatically."
- Clicking badge opens a right-side panel: Anchor manager (list of pins, audit trail, change pin, set expiry, rollback).

C) Anchor manager panel (right side modal) — wire elements and microcopy
- Header: Endpoint name — Anchored to vX.Y.Z
- Top row: small KPI strip: current latency / 95p latency / tokens-per-call / last-updated-by
- Main area: Pins timeline (visual): creation — canary windows — expiry — scheduled upgrade point (if any).
- Actions: [Change pinned version] [Schedule upgrade] [Set expiry] [Rollback] [Unanchor]
- Confirm modals: Keep copy concise and action-oriented. Examples:
  * Confirm rollback modal copy: "Rollback endpoint to v3.4.1 — This will route all requests to the selected version immediately. Canary traffic currently running will be canceled. Continue?"
  * Confirm unanchor: "Unanchor endpoint — the endpoint will resume following the recommended channel and may upgrade automatically. Are you sure?"
- Safety help text under actions: "Changing pins triggers a config deployment and may cause transient latency spikes. Use canary to reduce risk."

Edge cases & error states (notes for dev/QA):
- If a pinned version has been removed/deprecated from model registry: show badge “Pinned — version unavailable” and action "Migrate pin" with recommended replacement and impact summary.
- Network error during pin change: keep UI optimistic with spinner and allow manual retry. Provide guidance: "If you lose connectivity, the endpoint will continue serving the current pinned version."
- Pin expiry race: if expiry hits while a deployment is mid-update, timeline should show "expiry queued" and reconcile after deployment complete.

Backlog / implementation tickets (draft text for grooming):
- PI-887: pin expiry backend + API (include TTL on endpoint config) — acceptance: create a temporary pin and auto-unanchor on expiry.
- PI-901: pin audit trail events (who/when/change prev/new) surfaced in Anchor manager.
- PI-908: show model deltas (latency/cost delta) inline in model selector.
- UX-069: microcopy A/B test for pin tooltip and confirm flows.

Open questions / decisions needed:
1) Terminology: Anchor vs. Pin vs. Lock — prefer one. Proposal: use "Anchor" (verb: anchor, noun: anchor) — sentence: "Anchor endpoint to model version 3.4.6." Rationale: feels less technical than "pin" and avoids the connotation of immutability that "freeze" implies.
2) Default at create time: should anchor toggle default to off? Recommendation: default off for lower friction on new users; surface anchor as recommended for enterprise templates.
3) Canary UX: how many control knobs? Options: % traffic OR fixed request count. MVP: % traffic (1%, 5%, 10%) + duration.
4) Billing/cost display: show per-token delta near selector. Need API work (PI-908).

Microcopy library (single-line items for designers to drop into wires):
- Model selector title: "Choose a model version to anchor"
- Tooltip: "Anchoring locks this endpoint to a specific model version. Use scheduled upgrades to adopt improvements safely."
- Anchor badge label: "Anchored" (tooltip: "Pinned to v{version} — expires {date}")
- Floating badge label: "Floating" (tooltip: "Follows recommended channel")
- Button primary: "Create endpoint" / "Deploy update"
- Anchor manager header: "Anchor manager"
- Empty state (no anchors): "This endpoint is not anchored. Add an anchor to lock to a model version."

Acceptance criteria (minimal):
- User can anchor at endpoint creation and set expiry OR schedule an upgrade.
- Anchored state shown in endpoint list with correct badge + hovercard.
- Anchor manager shows audit trail entries for pin changes.
- Rollback action routes traffic to selected version and is auditable.

Quick TODOs (owner notes):
- Lina: mock 2 alternative wires for create step with anchor toggle on/off by Nov 10 (done) — iterate with design.
- Asha: draft copy variants for confirm modals and prepare A/B test matrix (by Nov 17).
- Miguel: check feasibility for per-token delta in selector and add API estimate in PI-908.
- Samir: add backend acceptance tests for pin expiry behavior (PI-887).

Notes-to-self / informal fragments:
- "If we go with ‘anchor’ we should update docs + SDK naming to avoid mismatch (client pin/unpin methods?)."
- "Consider exposing anchor intent in API as: anchor: {type: permanent|temporary|scheduled, expiry: iso, schedule_target: version}"
- "Think about mobile console: badge text might be abbreviated to ‘Anch’d’ — yuk. Keep mobile as icon+tooltip."

Related/prev work references:
- See product/console-and-rollouts/model-hub-quickpin-onboarding-copy-draft.json for onboarding copy (do not replicate language).

Next steps for grooming meeting:
- Walk through wires + copy with eng and SRE (20m).
- Decide terminology and default behavior (5m).
- Confirm API contract for expiry + audit trail (10m).
- Assignee selection for PI tickets and estimate.

This is a living doc — update as we lock decisions. Comments inline are fine.
